title: A guide to government securities for retail investors: Meaning, ways to invest, benefits and risks
body: Government securities (G-Secs) are debt instruments issued by the RBI on behalf of the central and state governments to raise funds from investors. These securities can be purchased in the primary market during government auctions or in the secondary market.
why: When RBI HIKES the REPO RATE → it becomes MORE EXPENSIVE for banks to borrow
Higher cost for banks → they increase loan interest rates for customers
More expensive EMIs → you borrow less for houses, cars, and businesses
Less borrowing → less spending → companies earn less profit
Company profits fall → stock market goes DOWN 📉
